accent.note: Text stop. 9.10:1 on the ground. Never a fill — white on it measures 1.97:1.

accent-fill.note: Fill stop. Carries white at 4.53:1. Shared unchanged across both themes.

accent-deep.note: Pressed and hover states on a filled surface. White at 6.23:1.

accent-ink.note: The light theme's text stop. 4.86:1 on its ground.

ground.note: Deliberately off the floor of the lightness range so a cast shadow has something beneath it to darken.

frost.note: Cool ramp — every step keeps B >= R, the inverse of the warm ramp it replaced. Lowest step still reaches 4.67:1 on the ground.

daylight.note: The light page. Its lifted surface goes to pure white — raised is lighter here, not darker.

slate.note: Light-theme foreground ramp. Lowest step reaches 4.64:1.

frost-ghost.note: Resting navigation and the table-of-contents rail. 4.67:1 — the lowest role in the system, still above AA body text.

cta-fg.note: White. It sits on --accent-fill, never on the bright text stop.

code-ground.note: The only surface that goes darker than the page, but narrower in reach than the name suggests. Expressive Code frames paint --bg-1 (#19262f dark, #ffffff light) at the shared 8px radius; this trio is consumed by bare <pre> blocks, of which the landing's install line is the only live instance.

code-ground-light.note: Code surfaces follow the theme. Pinning them dark made light-theme syntax tokens vanish into their own background — verified on `Record.Value` and `CompletedTask`.

aside-tip.note: 8.83:1. Not a brand token. Holds the same value as --outcome but is a separate declaration; see the Own-Your-Value Rule.

ink.note: Live. Colours D2 diagram text under the light theme. ThemeInspector.astro still lists it as unused; that entry is stale.

ink-dim.note: Live. Colours muted D2 diagram text under the light theme. Also stale in ThemeInspector.astro.

lit.note: The interaction hue. Hover and focus, nothing at rest. 11.74:1 on the ground. A text colour, never a fill. Sits 19 degrees off the caution callout, which holds only because the two never share a surface.

lit-light.note: The light-ground stop. 4.83:1 on Daylight; the dark stop would land at 1.3:1 here. Measured from the shipped hex rather than derived: 0.16 chroma leaves sRGB at this lightness, so the authored value clipped to 0.111 chroma at hue 86.

outcome.note: The payoff line on a capability card and the confirming tick beside a claim. Opens on the tip callout value but is a separate declaration, so retuning one cannot move the other. Never used in prose.

outcome-light.note: The light-ground stop, measured from the shipped hex. Holds the tip callout light value, as a separate declaration.

hueAudit.accentBand: Measured 239 / 253 / 256 degrees across the three stops — a 17-degree spread. surge.css:49 describes the family as 'locked at OKLCH 240 deg'; the lock is approximate, and the comment overstates it. The prior pairing it replaced spanned 37 degrees, so the tightening is real.
hueAudit.asideWheel: Isoluminant by construction. Dark: L 75.6-76.0%, C 0.146-0.150, hues 25 / 76 / 150 / 301. Light: L 51.9-52.8%, C 0.125-0.170, hues 25 / 58 / 147 / 300. Every hue sits at least 60 degrees off the accent band.

extensions.motionNotes: Easing is the `ease` keyword everywhere. No cubic-bezier, no steps, and no authored @keyframes exist in the site's own components. surge.css carries a global `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that collapses every animation and transition to 0.01ms with !important and forces scroll-behavior to auto, so the whole site is guarded at the root; the footer's local prefers-reduced-motion guard is redundant belt-and-braces. Third-party motion (the Starwind switch and the tw-animate-css select popup) declares no local duration or easing and inherits Tailwind defaults.

verification.probeNote: Programmatic .focus() is not a reliable way to verify :focus-visible in Chrome. Element.matches(':focus-visible') returned true while style resolution disagreed, which produced a false negative on four rules that were in fact applying. Every focus finding here was re-taken by pressing Tab, or by focusing then pressing Shift+Tab and Tab so the final landing was a genuine keyboard move.

narrative.overview:
An editorial page printed on blue-black stock, with one light source above it. Everything in this system follows from that image. Type does the work: the largest text carries the least weight, and each step down gains weight as it loses size, so hierarchy is read from proportion rather than from boxes, rules, or colour. Colour is rationed to a single azure family, and every emphasis in the interface is a percentage mix of it against transparency. Nothing is painted with an unrelated hue, so the whole page repaints from one small set of tokens.

The ground is deliberately not black. It sits at OKLCH lightness 20.4%, well off the floor of the range, because a cast shadow needs something beneath it to darken. At the bottom of the range nothing can be darker than the page and every elevation cue disappears at once. Raising the ground is what lets the system use real shadows, and the neutral ramps above it are cool throughout — every step keeps blue at or above red, because beside an azure accent a warm grey reads yellow-brown.

The accent is split rather than shaded. No single value can be both a legible link and a saturated fill on this ground, so the family carries three stops: a bright one for text, a saturated one for fills that must hold white, and a deeper one for pressed states. The register is restrained, editorial, and engineered. Confidence shows in the omissions that were made deliberately and recorded — the film grain was removed so dark fields stay flat, and the rule under the page title was removed because it read as a divider between a heading and its own first paragraph.
keyCharacteristics: One azure family, three stops, split by role rather than by shade
A raised ground, so shadow has somewhere to fall
Cool neutrals throughout; every step of both ramps clears 4.5:1
Flat fields, hairline borders, no boxes where a rule will do
One fixed radial wash as the sole ambient gradient
17px root, so every rem in the system is 17-based
Dark-first: bare :root is dark, light is the override

rules.name: The Text/Fill Split Rule
rules.body: --accent is a text colour and never a fill. --accent-fill is a fill and never text. The split is not cosmetic: on this ground the bright stop reads text at 9.10:1 but would put white at 1.97:1, and the fill stop carries white at 4.53:1 but would read as text at only 3.96:1. Reaching for the wrong stop breaks contrast in one direction or the other, every time.

rules.name: The Mix, Never Match Rule
rules.body: Every accent emphasis is written color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent…) N%, transparent). No emphasis colour is ever spelled as a literal. Text emphases mix from --accent; the hover ring mixes from --accent-fill.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: All accent stops sit in one narrow hue band — measured at 239, 253 and 256 degrees. There is no secondary brand colour: identity is carried by azure alone. When two things must be told apart within the brand, they are told apart by weight, size, position, or mix percentage. Gold and outcome are not exceptions to this, because neither states identity — see the Chrome-Only Rule.

rules.name: The Chrome-Only Rule
rules.body: --lit and --outcome live in chrome and never in prose. The hue wheel is full: five committed hues each wanting 60 degrees of separation is 600 degrees of demand on a 360 degree wheel, and the widest gap available gives 49. So a new value cannot clear every neighbour, and the question becomes which collision can never occur. --lit sits 19 degrees off the caution callout, and that is safe only because caution appears inside callouts and --lit only in chrome — the two never share a surface. Take either into a paragraph and the separation stops holding.

rules.name: The Own-Your-Value Rule
rules.body: A hue that sits near a callout must still be its own declaration. --outcome opens on the tip callout exact value, but as a separate token, because the four aside hues are matched in lightness within 1.07 of each other on the ground: brightening a shared value for a landing page would drag the tip callout out of that set, to 13.17:1 against danger 7.76:1. Two owners on one declaration means neither can be tuned.

rules.name: The Isoluminant Asides Rule
rules.body: The four callout hues are matched in lightness and chroma and separated by hue alone — dark at L 76% and C 0.15 across hues 25 / 76 / 150 / 301, light at L 52% across hues 25 / 58 / 147 / 300. Each sits at least 60 degrees off the accent band, so no callout title can be mistaken for a link, and each is far enough from the others to be told apart at a glance. They are not brand tokens and must not be promoted into the palette.

rules.name: The Inverse Weight Rule
rules.body: The largest type carries the least weight. Size falls and weight rises: 300 at 48px, 400 at 28px, 500 at 20px. This is the single most identifying property of the system, and it is why headings need no colour or rule to separate them.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Code Only Rule
rules.body: Fira Code sets code and nothing else. Uppercase index labels take the sans, because a monospace fixes every glyph to one advance, and the wide tracking an uppercase label wants then pushes the letters past the point where they read as words at all.

rules.name: The Reader Owns The Face Rule
rules.body: OpenDyslexic is a first-class option, not an afterthought. It runs 41% wider than Poppins at matched x-height, so its scope sets font-size-adjust: 0.397 — the measured width match — and the switch reflows no line. Code is exempt from the adjustment.

rules.name: The Two Rem Bases Rule
rules.body: Root font-size is 17px, so 1rem is 17px in every declaration — but @media resolves rem against the initial 16px while @container resolves it against the computed 17px. @media (min-width: 50rem) is 800px; @container (min-width: 18rem) is 306px. Never carry a breakpoint figure from one context to the other.

rules.name: The Raised Floor Rule
rules.body: The dark ground sits at OKLCH lightness 20.4%, deliberately off the bottom of the range, because a cast shadow needs something beneath it to darken. Never push the ground toward black to gain contrast: it removes every elevation cue in the system at once.

rules.name: The Edge Inverts Rule
rules.body: Elevation reverses with the theme. A raised dark surface is lighter than its ground and catches a highlight along its top edge, so the dark theme uses the inset edge and the shadow. A raised light surface cannot get meaningfully lighter than an already-near-white page, so the light theme drops the edge to transparent and the shadow carries alone.

rules.name: The One Wash Rule
rules.body: A page carries exactly one gradient and it belongs to the page or its hero, never to a component. Its strength is theme-specific and not symmetric: 12% on dark, 3% on light, because an accent wash over a near-white ground reads as a smudge rather than as light. The landing runs its own at 22% because that one is scoped to a hero, not to a whole page — home.css sets `body { background: var(--bg) }`, whose shorthand resets the docs theme's body background-image to none.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every structural border is 1px. Reach for 2px only for a focus outline or a selection marker, and for 3px only where an existing 3px marker already establishes the weight.

rules.name: The Lattice, Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Where a grid of related items is needed, draw single shared 1px borders conditionally per index at zero gap and zero radius, so the group reads as one ruled table. The landing's six-cell feature grid is the reference implementation. Do not turn it into cards.

dos: Do use --accent for text and --accent-fill for fills, every time. --accent-deep is the pressed state on a filled surface.
Do express every accent emphasis as color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent…) N%, transparent), so a hue change stays a token edit.
Do keep the dark ground off the floor of the lightness range. Shadow depends on it.
Do pair the inset light edge with the shadow on dark, and drop the edge on light.
Do keep the ambient wash accent-tinted and anchored to body, and keep its light-theme strength far below its dark-theme strength.
Do let size fall as weight rises. A heading is established by proportion, not by a rule or a colour.
Do give a focus ring a 2px accent outline with a 2px offset, and move the signal to the wrapper when the control itself must suppress its outline.
Do reserve borders in a transparent state when a state change would otherwise shift layout — the sidebar row and the social icon both do this.
Do hold every colour in surge.css. D2 diagrams, code frames, and Starwind components all resolve from it, and a colour written anywhere else stops following the theme toggle.
Do adopt the 42.5px / 1px / 8px / faint-tint contract for any new control added to the footer rail.
donts: Don't put --accent under white text or on a fill, and don't use --accent-fill as text. Each fails contrast in the opposite direction.

Don't introduce a hue outside the azure band for anything structural. Distinguish by weight, size, position, or mix percentage. --lit and --outcome are not structural: one marks the pointer, the other a claim, and both stay out of prose.
Don't take --lit or --outcome into a paragraph, a heading, or a callout. Their separation from the aside hues holds only because they never share a surface with them.
Don't point --outcome at the tip callout's variable, or the reverse. They may hold the same value; they may never be the same declaration.
Don't use the brand accent to mean "information", and don't spend --lit on anything at rest.
Don't pin a code surface to one theme. The syntax themes swap, and a pinned surface hides tokens that share its colour.
Don't put a gradient on a panel, card, button, or field. The system's one gradient belongs to the page.
Don't set a structural border above 1px. 2px is for focus and selection markers, and 3px only where a 3px marker already exists.
Don't write a colour as a literal hex outside the token block.
Don't carry a rem breakpoint figure between @media and @container. They resolve against different bases here.
Don't add a max-width that competes with --sl-content-width. It is the only lever on the reading column.

Don't ship a new interactive element with no focus style. Every control this project authors now rings at 2px --accent — 9.10:1 against the dark ground — with a 2px offset, or -2px where the element spans the full width of its container and a positive offset would draw off the edge. One element suppresses its own ring on purpose: the sidebar filter input, whose wrapper carries the signal instead. Starlight's own chrome, such as the skip link, keeps the browser default; that surface belongs to the framework, not to this system.

Don't add a step to the radius scale, and don't express one in rem. Every radius in the system is a literal pixel value drawn from 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 999. rem at a 17px root produced 8.5px and 6.8px values that read as a fourth and fifth step; they are gone.
